blurb: Cold-water oysters, mostly farmed. Tongyeong opens the harvest in mid to late October, the peak runs Nov-Feb, and one wiki says the fisheries ministry counts Nov-Apr as season. About 80% of output comes from the waters between Geoje and Tongyeong, and they spawn May-Sep.

eat: 꼬막 정식, cockle set meal in Beolgyo
blurb: A small ribbed clam, sold as chamkkomak and saekkomak. It runs Nov-Mar and spawns Jul-Sep. Goheung grows about 60% of the output, which irritates Beolgyo, the town whose name sells it.
caveat: One wiki puts the cockle festival in late Oct to early Nov. It ran Nov 1-3 in 2024 and Nov 21-23 in 2025. One community post says the season is Sep-Mar.

blurb: Scallops, including the red kind called hong-garibi. A wiki and the fisheries ministry both point to Nov-Dec, and the ministry picked scallops in four Novembers, including 2024 and 2025.
caveat: One magazine piece calls scallops a spring food, grilled or butter-steamed. The ministry's monthly picks track promotion, not harvest dates.

festivals: Hongseong Namdang Harbor Egg Cockle Festival (23rd), Jan 17-Feb 22, 2026
blurb: A bird-shaped cockle centred on Cheonsuman bay and Namdang Harbor. The window is Dec-Mar, and supply swings hard. The 2025 festival closed 21 days after opening, with about 10 t sold against 20+ t the year before.
caveat: The Korea Tourism listing shows the 2026 festival running to Apr 30, while the press says Feb 22. A Geoje fishing list puts the shellfish in spring.

blurb: A red-fleshed clam eaten raw. Harvest in Jinhae Bay starts in December, and sources say it runs into spring.
caveat: The end of the window is an estimate. One article says winter through spring and gives no month for the end.

blurb: Mussels, also called seop. One wiki gives Oct-Dec and a Geoje fishing list says winter. Both are single, low-authority sources.
caveat: The window rests on that wiki and one community list, so treat it as a lead.

blurb: Manila clams peak in Mar-Apr, and one wiki starts the season in February. The fishing statute lists no closed season for them.
A large fan-shaped clam that peaks Apr-May. The fisheries ministry has picked it in months from Apr to Jun, and harvest is closed Jul-Aug.
caveat: A Geoje fishing list places pen shell in winter, which no other source supports.

blurb: Tiny clams from the Seomjin River estuary around Hadong and Gwangyang. They peak May-Jun, and one magazine piece pairs them with a chive soup.
caveat: The same one magazine article says March, and a 2012 column says October.

blurb: A big hard clam best known in Buan, where it goes into a clear soup. Sources say spring, and one blog narrows that to Apr-May.
caveat: The window rests on one magazine piece and one blog. One wiki warns that eating it raw in summer carries risk.

blurb: A surf clam that spawns twice a year, so it has two windows. Spring runs Apr-May and autumn runs Oct-Nov. One source starts spring in March.
caveat: Both windows rest on weak sources.

blurb: Abalone is farmed, so supply runs nearly all year. One wiki says Aug-Oct, but the wild catch is closed Sep 1-Oct 31, and on Jeju Oct 1-Dec 31. The fisheries ministry has picked it in months from Feb to Jul.
caveat: The window is contested. It overlaps the wild closure, and farmed supply makes the fresh season nearly year-round.

blurb: A razor clam that fishers dig up by pouring salt into its hole. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, spring and summer, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.

eat: 유곽, stuffed grilled clam in Tongyeong
blurb: A large clam from the Yellow Sea and the South Sea. No source gives a season. The dish to know is Tongyeong's yugwak, a stuffed, grilled shell.
A short-neck clam. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, autumn and winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A large hard clam. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A clam that appears only on a Geoje fishing list, which says winter and gives no months. It stays off the calendar.
Turban shell snails. One wiki says Mar-Jun, while a Geoje fishing list names winter, spring and autumn.
caveat: The window rests on that one wiki.

blurb: A small abalone from Jeju. A Geoje fishing list says spring with no months, and the harvest is closed Jul-Aug on Jeju.
A freshwater river snail. One wiki gives May-Jun, and the fisheries ministry picked it in Jul 2023.
caveat: The window rests on that one wiki.

blurb: A whelk, called mullegodung in Korean. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A whelk, called gipeungol-mullegodung in Korean. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A large sea snail, called ppippul-godung in Korean. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, spring, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A whelk, called galsaekttimaemul-godung in Korean. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, spring, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A whelk from the West Sea, called keunguseul-ureong in Korean. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, spring, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A limpet, called satgat-jogae in Korean. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, spring, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A top shell snail, called bangseok-godung in Korean. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, summer, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.

eat: 간장게장, raw crab in soy sauce

closures.note: Practical dates. Local variants at Yeonpyeong and Baengnyeong

blurb: West Sea crab with two seasons a year. Females carry roe in spring, and males fill out in autumn. Boats stay in port through the summer closure, and retail price wars start the day it lifts.
caveat: Autumn 2026 was scarce, with males at 20,400 won/kg at Noryangjin. Autumn 2025 traded 5,716 t in its first month, a 10-year high.

closures.note: East of 131°30'E. Elsewhere it runs to Nov 30, and females are banned all year

festivals: Uljin Snow Crab and Red Snow Crab Festival, Feb 27-Mar 2, 2026
blurb: East Coast snow crab, with Yeongdeok and Uljin as the best-known ports. Law sets the edges of the season, and festivals run late Feb to late Mar. Yeongdeok's Gangu port held its first auction on Nov 3, 2025, with a top bid of 169,000 won for one crab.
caveat: No source states peak months, so Dec-Mar is an estimate. Crab sold in early November likely comes from offshore grounds that open Nov 1.

blurb: A deeper-water cousin of the snow crab. A Geoje fishing list says spring and autumn, with no months. The harvest is closed Jul 10-Aug 25.

festivals: Hongseong Namdang Harbor Fleshy Prawn Festival (31st), Sep 4-Nov 8, 2026
blurb: A wild West Sea prawn sold in autumn, often grilled in salt. It runs Sep-Dec, the fisheries ministry picked it in Sep and Oct, and the Namdang Harbor festival runs into early November. The harvest is closed May-Jun.
caveat: Nobody has sourced how much of the festival shrimp is actually farmed whiteleg shrimp.

blurb: Korea's top farmed shrimp. Farms switched to it after white spot virus wiped out many fleshy prawn (daeha) farms. A green tail tip means daeha and red means whiteleg. One wiki sees little taste difference and a much lower price.
caveat: Pond harvest months are unsourced. A ministry text calls it an autumn item, alongside daeha.

blurb: An umbrella name for three shrimp, kkotsaeu, dakssaeu and dohwasaeu, from around Ulleungdo and Dokdo. A Geoje fishing list puts kkotsaeu and dohwasaeu in winter, with no months.
One of the shrimp sold as Dokdo shrimp around Ulleungdo and Dokdo. A tourism article gives Sep-Dec.
caveat: The window rests on that one tourism article.

blurb: A prawn sold live as odori. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, spring and summer, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A small sweet shrimp eaten raw. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A small shrimp also called gasibalsaeu. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A crab used mainly for gejang, crab marinated in soy sauce or chili. It spawns Jun-Aug, and no eating season turned up. Incheon reports no closure beyond protecting females with eggs.
A crab that lives north of Goseong on the East Coast. No season turned up, and the only month claim is a low-grade comment calling imported Russian horsehair crab a spring item.
Imported crab with no real season. Weak sources give Oct-Jan, Jun-Sep, or after Chuseok (the autumn harvest holiday) to mid-Nov. Availability follows the import price.
caveat: The sources contradict each other.

blurb: A barnacle. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A barnacle shaped like a turtle's hand. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.

festivals: Muchangpo Webfoot Octopus and Flounder Festival, Mar 20-Apr 5, 2026
blurb: A small octopus caught in spring, when females carry eggs. The closure starts May 11, which caps the spring window by law, and fishing reopens Sep 1. The fisheries ministry never picked it in 61 months of monthly picks.
caveat: One wiki says April. One column says autumn tastes better, and the saying goes "bom jukkumi, gaeul nakji" (spring webfoot octopus, autumn long-arm octopus).

blurb: A long-armed octopus tied to autumn by the saying "bom jukkumi, gaeul nakji" (spring webfoot octopus, autumn long-arm octopus). No source gives a month, so Oct is an estimate.
caveat: No month appears in any source, and the closure date differs by province.

blurb: The big octopus. No source gives a month. The fisheries ministry picked it in Aug 2024 and Jul 2025, and a Geoje fishing list says summer and winter.
The common squid. A Geoje fishing list says summer, with no months. Gangwon province says the fish moved north as the sea warmed.

A small squid with a Jun-Oct fishing season and a July peak. The only source is a fishing-season site, which says nothing about food. Jeju's changojingeo and the East Sea's hwasalchogojingeo both go by the name.
caveat: The window comes from a fishing-season source, not a food one.

blurb: Cuttlefish. A Geoje fishing list says spring and autumn, with no months, and the fisheries ministry picked it in May 2025. It has no row in the closed-season table.
A small squid. Only a Geoje fishing list gives seasons, winter and summer, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A small squid also sold as banwonni-kkolttugi. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
A reef squid also called huin-ojingeo. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, summer, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.

A sea squirt eaten raw. Farmed stock ships from April and peaks May-Jun, with about two thirds from Tongyeong and Geoje. Wild stock peaks from after Chuseok, the autumn harvest holiday, through November.
caveat: One wiki says May, and the fisheries ministry picked Mar-Apr. One undated report says heat and low-oxygen water hurt 60-70% of Tongyeong farmers.

blurb: A warty sea squirt eaten raw for only about two months, from late March to early May. Jindong Bay in Changwon is the production centre.
caveat: One restaurant owner gave those dates. One wiki says April.

blurb: A small sea squirt. Only a Geoje fishing list gives a season, winter, with no months, so it stays off the calendar.
Sea cucumber. One wiki says Oct-Nov and a Geoje fishing list says winter and autumn. The harvest is closed in July.
caveat: The window rests on that wiki and one community list.

blurb: Sea urchin. A Geoje fishing list puts the purple urchin in spring and summer, and malttong-seongge in autumn and winter, with no months. Tongyeong restaurants serve it over rice, with gaps out of season.
A spoon worm eaten raw or grilled. One wiki says winter, with the south coast best, though it is dug all year. The months are an estimate from that season word.
caveat: One wiki page gives the season, and no other source was found.

blurb: Fresh laver, called mulgim, is auctioned from mid November to late April. Sinan held its first sale on Nov 18 for the 2026 crop, and Haenam's auctions ran to about Apr 23 in 2025.
A hair-fine green seaweed, fresh from late November to February. Its texture and aroma fade after February, and it is sold frozen all year.
caveat: One source says Dec-Apr. The fisheries ministry picked it in Jan 2026.

festivals: Gijang Sea Mustard and Kelp Festival, Apr 17-19, 2026
blurb: Sea mustard, harvested mostly in winter and spring. Seafood expert Kim Ji-min says it is best from February into early spring. Jindo, Wando, Tongyeong and Geoje are the main areas.
caveat: Sources give seasons, not months, so Dec-Apr is an estimate.

blurb: A green seaweed that grows near fresh-water inflow on the upper shore. One wiki gives Nov-Mar.
caveat: The window rests on that one wiki page.

blurb: A seaweed whose name is unsettled. One wiki says Dec-Mar, while a Wando seller starts in mid February because January plants are too soft.
caveat: What markets sell as gamtae may be gasiparae, a different plant.

blurb: A brown seaweed of the east and south coasts, blanched and eaten as a wrap with chojang dipping sauce. Sources say winter, or March, so Jan-Mar is an estimate.
caveat: One wiki says winter and a news site says March.

blurb: Hijiki, harvested Mar-May. It is closed Oct-Jan, so the winter label in older press is wrong.
caveat: The window rests on one wiki alone.

blurb: A thin red seaweed. One wiki says it can be harvested except in winter, with an early spring peak, and gives no months.
Kelp. Wando's harvest runs early May to early July, so it is not a winter crop. The fisheries ministry picked it in Jun 2025 and May 2026.
